title_original: Robert Pattinson’s journey from Harry Potter and Twilight to James Bond: ‘The honour of a lifetime’
excerpt_original: The 40-year-old British actor has had a remarkable career and is back again with the coveted 007 New James Bond announced ... and the name’s Pattinson, Robert Pattinson Robert Pattinson’s gift for cool, sensual menace makes him an exquisite choice as James Bond There are big…

blocks.text: There are big years in an actor’s career, and then there is Robert Pattinson ’s 2026.

This year the 40-year-old Brit has been the face of everything from Kristoffer Borgli’s relationship satire The Drama to Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey and Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime. Now, in the culmination of a remarkable run, he has landed the most coveted role in British cinema: James Bond.

After weeks of intense speculation , on Monday the official Bond accounts confirmed Pattinson as the seventh actor to play 007. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said.

Pattinson was easily the most famous of the contenders, and an unusual one: an arthouse actor with a franchise heartthrob’s profile. “Is Robert Pattinson the last true movie star?” the New York Times asked in 2024.
Pattinson landed his first big film role more than two decades ago, playing Cedric Diggory in 2005’s Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire .

links.text: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire

blocks.text: He became a household name at 21, when he was cast opposite Kristen Stewart in the first of five Twilight films. The pair played star-crossed lovers Edward Cullen, a vampire, and Bella Swan, a mortal – turning Pattinson into a global teen pin-up.

blocks.alt: Three teens sitting with four of them standing
blocks.caption: Pictured from left to right, starting at top left, are Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire actors Katie Leung, Stanislav Ianevski, Clémence Poésy, Robert Pattinson, Rupert Grint, Daniel Radcliffe and Emma Watson. Photograph: Dave Hogan/Getty Images

blocks.text: The on-screen romance also became a real-life one: the pair dated for four years, as the films became a global phenomenon, eventually taking more than $3.3bn at the worldwide box office. Even Donald Trump tweeted his thoughts about their relationship.

“He’s a real movie star, and that was clear the minute he appears in the first Twilight ,” veteran film journalist Steven Gaydos told the Guardian this summer. “Their mutual star power obscured the franchise’s loopy werewolves-and-vampires silliness and kept the focus on love and heat between two major new charismatic movie stars.”
Pattinson was born in Barnes, south-west London, the youngest of three children. His father traded in classic cars; his mother worked for a modelling agency.

He first became interested in acting as a schoolboy, joining amateur drama group the Barnes theatre club. “I wouldn’t be acting if it wasn’t for that little club,” he said in 2008. “I went originally because a lot of pretty girls went there.”

blocks.alt: A boy and girl dancing with string lights behind them
blocks.caption: Robert Pattinson and Kristen Stewart in Twilight. Photograph: Summit Entertainment/Sportsphoto/Allstar

blocks.text: He worked backstage until “all the good people left and I was the only one tall enough to play the lead”, he said.

In the years after Twilight, Pattinson largely avoided the conventional route toward Hollywood leading man status, gravitating instead toward some of the more challenging independent film-makers. He was in David Cronenberg’s Cosmopolis (2012) as a billionaire whose limousine journey across Manhattan becomes an existential fever dream, and James Gray’s The Lost City of Z (2016), as a moustachioed British explorer in the Amazon.

The real turning point was the Safdie brothers’ nocturnal thriller Good Time (2017), in which he played Connie Nikas, a small-time New York criminal desperate to get his brother out of prison. Pattinson’s performance established him as one of his generation’s most exciting actors.
Claire Denis’s High Life (2018) followed, then Robert Eggers’s The Lighthouse (2019), in which he played a 19th-century lighthouse keeper descending into madness opposite Willem Dafoe.

blocks.alt: Man in red coat with gray hoodie on underneath it looks straight ahead in a hallway with square ceiling lights
blocks.caption: Robert Pattinson in Good Time. Photograph: A24/Allstar

blocks.text: It was Nolan’s Tenet (2020) that marked Pattinson’s return to blockbusters. In it, he played Neil, a mysterious, impeccably dressed intelligence operative whose dry wit made him one of the film’s most engaging presences. Fans have been circulating clips this week as evidence he’d make a fitting Bond.

Two years later, Pattinson played a younger, more psychologically tortured Bruce Wayne in Matt Reeves’s The Batman. The film was a commercial hit, while the Guardian said Pattinson played the “brooding” role with “appealing vulnerability”.

Since then he has alternated between studio films and idiosyncratic projects: in Bong Joon Ho’s Mickey 17 (2025) he played multiple versions of a hapless worker whose job is to die and be regenerated, and in Die My Love, opposite Jennifer Lawrence, a husband struggling to understand his wife’s crisis after motherhood.
This year has been busier still. In The Drama , Pattinson starred opposite Zendaya as Charlie, an art curator whose engagement is thrown into turmoil by a revelation about his fiancée’s past.

blocks.caption: Robert Pattinson and Zendaya in The Drama. Photograph: AP

blocks.text: In The Odyssey he was Antinous, villainous suitor to Anne Hathaway’s Penelope. “He absolutely stole the show for me,” wrote US critic Erik Davis, and his oily delivery of “get these beggars out of here” spawned multiple memes. Most recently, as To Catch a Predator presenter Chris Hansen in Primetime, he has fuelled Oscar speculation: The Independent called it “Oscar-worthy”, the Times “superb”.
“He’s drifted back toward commercial cinema,” Variety chief critic Guy Lodge told the Guardian this summer . “But he’s now a looser, more interesting actor for his arthouse dabblings.”

Bond will leave little time to rest. Dune: Part Three, in which he plays the shapeshifting conspirator Scytale, is due in December, and a sequel to The Batman is reportedly scheduled for 2028. Though he does have a head start: Denis Villeneuve directs both Dune and the next 007 film, and Pattinson has said working with him was “never really a stress”.

blocks.alt: Pattinson in the upcoming Dune: Part Three.
blocks.caption: Pattinson in the upcoming Dune: Part Three. Photograph: Courtesy Warner Bros. Pictures

blocks.text: Away from the screen, Pattinson keeps his private life private. After relationships with Stewart and the singer FKA twigs, he is now with the actor and musician Suki Waterhouse, with whom he has a young daughter.

Fame has not always been easy: “Nothing, I don’t think, can prepare you for the fans,” he said during Twilight mania. “I’m completely overwhelmed every time.” The role of Bond is likely to bring that level of attention back on an even greater scale.
